title: Chats over several library papers
acceptance_criteria: Given any chat, at any time, when the user types @ in the chat composer, then the same paper picker as on the home page lets them add any number of ready library papers or remove included ones; the included papers show as removable chips at the top of the chat, and beyond three they collapse into "+N more", which lists every paper with its remove button.
Given the paper whose id is in the chat's URL is removed, when the chat updates, then it re-routes to /papers/{new first paper}/chats/{chatId}; the last remaining paper cannot be removed.
Given a chat with several papers, when any of those papers is opened, then the chat appears in its chat list.
Given a question over several papers, when evidence is retrieved, then every included paper gets a fair share of the context and comparisons cite each relevant paper.
Given a citation to a document outside the chat's papers, when the answer is validated, then it fails as today.
Given a paper removed from a chat, when history is viewed, then earlier answers keep their citations, and the chat no longer appears under that paper.
Given existing single-paper chats, when the migration runs, then each becomes a one-paper chat with its pinned PDF and unchanged history.

Given a comparative question over several papers, when the planner runs, then it produces sub-questions only for the papers the comparison targets, at most five, retrieves each within its paper's documents, and synthesizes one answer that cites each paper.
Given the papers in a chat, when retrieval runs, then all of them use the same embedding model, so one filtered vector search spans them.

Given EXPERIMENTAL_OPEN_MODELS is off, when multi-paper chats are used, then only hosted models apply; with the flag on, multi-paper chats are unavailable to local models while open models stay frozen.
Given an answer citing several papers, when it renders, then each citation names its paper and page.

Given a citation to a paper other than the one in the reader, when it is clicked, then the reader opens that paper's PDF in a new tab (or focuses its existing tab) at the cited passage; the user can switch between tabs and close any tab except the last.
Given a multi-paper chat, when it is opened or linked from any of its papers, then its URL is /papers/{first paper in the chat's list}/chats/{chatId}.

Given any multi-paper question on a hosted model, when the prompt is assembled, then it goes through the existing budgeted assembly (assemble_answer_prompt or its successor). Instructions, question and history shares keep their caps, and the evidence budget is split across papers with a per-paper floor, so the request never exceeds the hosted working budget (HOSTED_WORKING_CONTEXT_TOKENS).

Given five papers, a long conversation and a comparative question, when every planner, sub-question and synthesis call is assembled, then none raises CONTEXT_LIMIT. Paper summaries and headers enter prompts only as bounded short headers, never as full summaries.

Given the design in docs/plans/retrieval-orchestration.md, when multi-paper evidence is allocated, then each paper in scope gets its floor while floors fit, papers beyond what fits are routed by relevance, and each rule cites its source in code comments or the design doc.
Given more papers than floors fit, when evidence is allocated, then the most relevant papers by their best reranked score answer, and the others add nothing to that turn, with no padding.

Given a question that names an included paper by its title, as its chip names it ("Surname Year"), or with an @ mention the composer inserts when the paper is added by typing @, when evidence is allocated, then that paper is always kept.

Given a chat over thirty papers, when a question is admitted and answered, then admission and search run the same number of database statements as for three papers, the candidate pool has a fixed size, every model call stays within its budget, routing selects by relevance, and named papers are kept.
test_cases: Migration upgrade/backfill test from 0007 with existing chats.
Retrieval across documents with per-paper shares of a bounded list and mixed embedding profiles.
Citation validation across chat documents; foreign documents rejected.
Frontend: multi-select picker, paper chips, cross-paper citation reader switch, chat listed under each paper.
Budget test: five papers, a long history at the compaction limit and a comparative question; every assembled call stays within the input budget, with a per-paper evidence floor.
Large N: thirty papers with statement counts, budgets, relevance routing and a named paper; the API accepts more than five papers; chips collapse in the UI.
verification: Implemented 2026-10-10 on feat/ara-088-multi-paper-chats in the isolated ara-multi-test project, then merged with ARA-093 (feat/ux-feedback-round 874db2a) and reworked for any number of papers. Final: python3 scripts/test-stack.py test --project-name ara-multi-test: Ruff clean, 1083 passed in 220.1 s. Frontend npm run check: 603 tests in 78 files (after the picker follow-up); npm run build passed (existing chunk-size warning). Fixture unittests: 26 OK. Evidence per criterion: picker without a limit, collapsing chips, removal and rerouting, canonical URL and listing under every paper (multi-paper.test.tsx, App.test.tsx, PaperPicker.test.tsx, test_chat_papers_integration.py); floors while they fit, relevance routing, named papers kept (test_multi_paper_packing.py, test_multi_paper_budget_integration.py, test_multi_paper_scale_integration.py); 30 papers run the same statements as 3 for admission and retrieval, within budget (test_multi_paper_scale_integration.py); comparative sub-questions capped at five, bounded planner list (test_query_planner.py, test_multi_paper_answers_integration.py); foreign citations rejected; migration backfill and downgrade (test_chat_papers_migration.py); one embedding model with bounded filtered searches (test_retrievers_integration.py); local models refused with the flag on; paper-named citation chips and reader tabs (multi-paper.test.tsx, reader-tabs.test.tsx). Not run: the Playwright journey e2e/multi-paper.spec.ts, live OpenAI calls and a visual browser check. Not measured on the user's papers, as the design says.
